done_when: The worker brief lets a worker change a file outside its Scope that the change needs, naming each such file and why in its handoff, and the review reports only outside-Scope files the work doesn't need; workers still stop for a one-way step, a security question, a new moving part or contradicting Done-when items. The brief and the review ask for an end-to-end test only for items that change runtime behaviour; settings, docs, deletions and test-only items are proven by the check the item names. The brief tells workers to name new test files after the behaviour they prove, never after the fix's slug.

findings.body: The brief still says at lines 101–103 to write a test at the user boundary for every Done-when item, then run it and watch it fail. That applies even when a settings, docs, deletion, or test-only item names a different check. The new runtime-only rule at lines 112–115 therefore does not remove the extra test requirement that this fix is meant to remove.
findings.title: Not done: Nonruntime items still require a new boundary test

findings.body: This command-level test checks for the new conditional sentence but passes while the generated brief still unconditionally requires a new boundary test for each item at src/forge/templates/brief.md:101–103. It does not catch the remaining contradiction in the behavior it names.

why: Workers stop and ask before every file outside their Scope, even a caller or type file the change plainly needs, and the brief demands an end-to-end test for every item even for docs, settings, deletions and test-only changes, so workers and reviews waste rounds
